sets.title: Calls between six friends
sets.contentHtml:
Anu, Bijay, Chetan, Deepak, Eshan, and Faruq are six friends. Each of them uses a mobile number from exactly one of the two mobile operators - Xitel and Yocel. During the last month, the six friends made several calls to each other. Each call was made by one of these six friends to another. The table below summarizes the number of minutes of calls that each of the six made to (outgoing minutes) and received from (incoming minutes) these friends, grouped by the operators. sets.title: Travellers and four currencies
sets.contentHtml:
Aurevia, Brelosia, Cyrenia and Zerathania are four countries with their currencies being Aurels, Brins, Crowns, and Zentars, respectively. The currencies have different exchange values. Crown’s currency exchange rate with Zentars = 0.5, i.e., 1 Crown is worth 0.5 Zentars.

Three travelers, Jano, Kira, and Lian set out from Zerathania visiting exactly two of the countries. Each country is visited by exactly two travelers. Each traveler has a unique Flight Cost, which represents the total cost of airfare in traveling to both the countries and back to Zerathania. The Flight Cost of Jano was 4000 Zentars, while that of the other two travelers were 5000 and 6000 Zentars, not necessarily in that order.

When visiting a country, a traveler spent either 1000, 2000 or 3000 in the country’s local currency. Each traveler had different spends (in the country’s local currency) in the two countries he/she visited. Across all the visits, there were exactly two spends of 1000 and exactly one spend of 3000 (in the country’s local currency).

The total “Travel Cost” for a traveler is the sum of his/her Flight Cost and the money spent in the countries visited.

The citizens of the four countries with knowledge of these travels made a few observations, with spends measured in their respective local currencies:

  1. Aurevia citizen: Jano and Kira visited our country, and their Travel Costs were 3500 and 8000, respectively.
  2. Brelosia citizen: Kira and Lian visited our country, spending 2000 and 3000, respectively. Kira’s Travel Cost was 4000.
  3. Cyrenia citizen: Lian visited our country and her Travel Cost was 36000.

sets.title: Puzzle-solving competition
sets.contentHtml:
Anirbid, Chandranath, Koushik, and Suranjan participated in a puzzle solving competition. The competition comprised 10 puzzles that had to be solved in the same sequence, i.e., a competitor got access to a puzzle as soon as they solved the previous puzzle. Some of the puzzles were visual puzzles and the others were number-based puzzles. The winner of the competition was the one who solved all puzzles in the least time.

The following charts describe their progress in the competition. The first chart (“All puzzles”) shows the number of puzzles solved by each competitor at a given time (in minutes) after the start of the competition. The second chart (“Visual puzzles”) shows the number of visual puzzles solved by each competitor at a given time (in minutes) after the start of the competition.

sets.title: Trade among P, X, C and ROW
sets.contentHtml:
Three countries — Pumpland (P), Xiland (X) and Cheeseland (C) — trade among themselves and with the (other countries in) Rest of World (ROW). All trade volumes are given in IC (international currency). The following terminology is used:

  • Trade balance = Exports – Imports
  • Total trade = Exports + Imports
  • Normalized trade balance = Trade balance / Total trade, expressed in percentage terms

The following information is known.

  1. The normalized trade balances of P, X and C are 0%, 10%, and –20%, respectively.
  2. 40% of exports of X are to P. 22% of imports of P are from X.
  3. 90% of exports of C are to P; 4% are to ROW.
  4. 12% of exports of ROW are to X, 40% are to P.
  5. The export volumes of P, in IC, to X and C are 600 and 1200, respectively. P is the only country that exports to C.

sets.title: Passing the Buck
sets.contentHtml:
Seven children, Aarav, Bina, Chirag, Diya, Eshan, Farhan, and Gaurav, are sitting in a circle facing inside (not necessarily in the same order) and playing a game of ‘Passing the Buck’.

The game is played over 10 rounds. In each round, the child holding the Buck must pass it directly to a child sitting in one of the following positions:

  • Immediately to the left;
  • Immediately to the right;

questions.stemHtml: What was the duration of calls (in minutes) from Bijay to Anu?
questions.solutionHtml:
Key deductions. Anu and Bijay are the only Xitel users, so Anu’s outgoing-to-Xitel (100) is all Anu→Bijay, and Anu’s incoming-from-Xitel (50) is all Bijay→Anu.

Everything Yocel users receive from Xitel was sent by Anu or Bijay: 250 + 275 + 100 + 100 = 725 = Anu→Yocel + Bijay→Yocel = Anu→Yocel + 200, so Anu→Yocel = 525.

Yocel-to-Yocel calls: total received 150 + 100 + 375 + 150 = 775 = total sent 175 + 150 + 100 + Faruq→Yocel, so Faruq→Yocel = 350.

Bijay→Anu is Anu’s whole incoming-from-Xitel figure, since Bijay is the only other Xitel user: 50 minutes.

questions.stemHtml: What was the duration of calls (in minutes) from Deepak to Chetan?
questions.solutionHtml:
Key deductions. Anu and Bijay are the only Xitel users, so Anu’s outgoing-to-Xitel (100) is all Anu→Bijay, and Anu’s incoming-from-Xitel (50) is all Bijay→Anu.

Everything Yocel users receive from Xitel was sent by Anu or Bijay: 250 + 275 + 100 + 100 = 725 = Anu→Yocel + Bijay→Yocel = Anu→Yocel + 200, so Anu→Yocel = 525.

Yocel-to-Yocel calls: total received 150 + 100 + 375 + 150 = 775 = total sent 175 + 150 + 100 + Faruq→Yocel, so Faruq→Yocel = 350.

Using the “no calls” facts among Yocel users: Deepak receives from Yocel only from Faruq (Chetan→Deepak = Eshan→Deepak = 0), so Faruq→Deepak = 100. Faruq→Yocel = 350 with Faruq→Eshan = 200 gives Faruq→Chetan = 50. Chetan receives from Yocel only from Deepak and Faruq (Eshan→Chetan = 0): Deepak→Chetan + 50 = 150, so Deepak→Chetan = 100.

Check: Deepak→Yocel = 150 = Deepak→Chetan + Deepak→Eshan (Deepak→Faruq = 0), so Deepak→Eshan = 50, and Eshan then receives Chetan 125 + Deepak 50 + Faruq 200 = 375 from Yocel, as given. Answer: 100.

questions.stemHtml: What is the sum of Travel Costs for all travelers in Zentars?
questions.solutionHtml:
Who visited where. 3 travellers × 2 countries = 6 visits, and each of Aurevia, Brelosia and Cyrenia gets exactly two. Aurevia: Jano, Kira. Brelosia: Kira, Lian. So Cyrenia: Jano, Lian.

Spends (local currency). The single 3000 is Lian in Brelosia; Kira spent 2000 in Brelosia. Kira’s two spends differ, so Kira spent 1000 in Aurevia. The remaining spends are one 1000 and two 2000s for Jano-Aurevia, Jano-Cyrenia and Lian-Cyrenia; Jano’s two spends differ, so Lian spent 2000 in Cyrenia and Jano spent 1000 and 2000 in some order.

Rates. Kira’s Travel Cost is 8000 Aurels = 4000 Brins, so 1 Brin = 2 Aurels. Let 1 Aurel = a Zentars (1 Brin = 2a, 1 Crown = 0.5).

Kira: 8000a = Flight + 1000a + 2000(2a) → FlightK = 3000a. Jano: 3500a = 4000 + spends. If Jano spent 2000 in Aurevia and 1000 in Cyrenia: 3500a = 4000 + 2000a + 500 → a = 3, giving FlightK = 9000 – impossible. So Jano spent 1000 Aurels and 2000 Crowns: 3500a = 4000 + 1000a + 1000 → a = 2.

Thus 1 Aurel = 2 Z, 1 Brin = 4 Z, 1 Crown = 0.5 Z; FlightK = 6000 Z, so FlightL = 5000 Z. Check Lian: 5000 + 3000×4 + 2000×0.5 = 18000 Z = 36000 Crowns ✓.

Travel Costs in Zentars: Jano 4000 + 2000 + 1000 = 7000; Kira 6000 + 2000 + 8000 = 16000; Lian 18000. Sum = 41000.

questions.stemHtml: How much is exported from C to X, in IC?
questions.solutionHtml:
C first. C imports only from P, so C’s imports = 1200. Normalised balance −20%: (EC − 1200)/(EC + 1200) = −0.2 → EC = 800. C exports: 90% → P = 720, 4% → ROW = 32, the remaining 6% → X = 48.

Unknowns: EX (X’s exports) and R (ROW’s total exports). P’s imports IP = 0.4EX (from X) + 720 (from C) + 0.4R (from ROW). X’s imports IX = 600 + 48 + 0.12R.

X’s balance +10% → EX − IX = 0.1(EX + IX) → EX = (11/9)IX. And 0.4EX = 0.22IP.

Solving: R = 2100, IX = 648 + 252 = 900, EX = 1100, IP = 440 + 720 + 840 = 2000 (and 22% of 2000 = 440 ✓). P’s balance is 0, so EP = 2000 = 600 + 1200 + P→ROW, giving P→ROW = 200.

ROW’s exports of 2100: 252 to X, 840 to P, 0 to C, so ROW→ROW = 1008. X’s exports of 1100: 440 to P, 0 to C, so X→ROW = 660.

C→X = 6% of 800 = 48.

questions.stemHtml: Who is sitting immediately to the right of Bina?
questions.solutionHtml:
Set-up. Number the seats 0–6 round the circle so that “left” means +1 and “right” means −1 (same convention for everyone, since all face inside). Put Bina at 0.

R1 left 1 → Aarav at 1. R2 right 2 → seat 6. R3 right 1 → Diya at 5. R5 ends at Aarav (1). R6 left 2 → seat 3. R7 left 1 → Gaurav at 4. R8 left 1 → seat 5 = Diya.

Chirag, Eshan and Farhan fill seats 2, 3 and 6. R9 goes from Diya (5) to Farhan, so Farhan is within two seats of 5: seat 3 or 6. R10 goes from Farhan to Chirag (within two seats). If Farhan = 6, Chirag would have to be at 2 or 3 – neither is within two of 6. So Farhan = 3, Chirag = 2, Eshan = 6.

Seating (going left from Bina): Bina, Aarav, Chirag, Farhan, Gaurav, Diya, Eshan.

Passes: R1 B→A (L1), R2 A→E (R2), R3 E→D (R1), R4 D→?, R5 ?→A, R6 A→F (L2), R7 F→G (L1), R8 G→D (L1), R9 D→F (R2), R10 F→C (R1). For R4–R5 the middle child must be within two seats of both Diya (5) and Aarav (1): Farhan (R2, R2), Eshan (L1, L2) or Bina (L2, L1) – all three possible.

Immediately right of Bina = seat 0 − 1 = seat 6 = Eshan.

questions.stemHtml: Who is sitting third to the left of Eshan?
questions.solutionHtml:
Set-up. Number the seats 0–6 round the circle so that “left” means +1 and “right” means −1 (same convention for everyone, since all face inside). Put Bina at 0.

R1 left 1 → Aarav at 1. R2 right 2 → seat 6. R3 right 1 → Diya at 5. R5 ends at Aarav (1). R6 left 2 → seat 3. R7 left 1 → Gaurav at 4. R8 left 1 → seat 5 = Diya.

Chirag, Eshan and Farhan fill seats 2, 3 and 6. R9 goes from Diya (5) to Farhan, so Farhan is within two seats of 5: seat 3 or 6. R10 goes from Farhan to Chirag (within two seats). If Farhan = 6, Chirag would have to be at 2 or 3 – neither is within two of 6. So Farhan = 3, Chirag = 2, Eshan = 6.

Passes: R1 B→A (L1), R2 A→E (R2), R3 E→D (R1), R4 D→?, R5 ?→A, R6 A→F (L2), R7 F→G (L1), R8 G→D (L1), R9 D→F (R2), R10 F→C (R1). For R4–R5 the middle child must be within two seats of both Diya (5) and Aarav (1): Farhan (R2, R2), Eshan (L1, L2) or Bina (L2, L1) – all three possible.

Eshan is at seat 6; third to the left = 6 + 3 = 9 ≡ seat 2 = Chirag.

questions.stemHtml: For which of the following pass types can the total number of occurrences be uniquely determined?
questions.solutionHtml:
Set-up. Number the seats 0–6 round the circle so that “left” means +1 and “right” means −1 (same convention for everyone, since all face inside). Put Bina at 0.

R1 left 1 → Aarav at 1. R2 right 2 → seat 6. R3 right 1 → Diya at 5. R5 ends at Aarav (1). R6 left 2 → seat 3. R7 left 1 → Gaurav at 4. R8 left 1 → seat 5 = Diya.

Chirag, Eshan and Farhan fill seats 2, 3 and 6. R9 goes from Diya (5) to Farhan, so Farhan is within two seats of 5: seat 3 or 6. R10 goes from Farhan to Chirag (within two seats). If Farhan = 6, Chirag would have to be at 2 or 3 – neither is within two of 6. So Farhan = 3, Chirag = 2, Eshan = 6.

Seating (going left from Bina): Bina, Aarav, Chirag, Farhan, Gaurav, Diya, Eshan.

Passes: R1 B→A (L1), R2 A→E (R2), R3 E→D (R1), R4 D→?, R5 ?→A, R6 A→F (L2), R7 F→G (L1), R8 G→D (L1), R9 D→F (R2), R10 F→C (R1). For R4–R5 the middle child must be within two seats of both Diya (5) and Aarav (1): Farhan (R2, R2), Eshan (L1, L2) or Bina (L2, L1) – all three possible.

Fixed rounds give L1 × 3 (R1, R7, R8), R2 × 2 (R2, R9), R1 × 2 (R3, R10), L2 × 1 (R6). Rounds 4–5 add either R2 + R2 (via Farhan) or L1 + L2 (via Eshan or Bina). So L1 is 3 or 4, R2 is 4 or 2, L2 is 1 or 2, but Immediately to the right is always 2 – the only one fixed.

questions.stemHtml: For which of the following children is it possible to determine how many times they received the Buck?
questions.solutionHtml:
Set-up. Number the seats 0–6 round the circle so that “left” means +1 and “right” means −1 (same convention for everyone, since all face inside). Put Bina at 0.

R1 left 1 → Aarav at 1. R2 right 2 → seat 6. R3 right 1 → Diya at 5. R5 ends at Aarav (1). R6 left 2 → seat 3. R7 left 1 → Gaurav at 4. R8 left 1 → seat 5 = Diya.

Chirag, Eshan and Farhan fill seats 2, 3 and 6. R9 goes from Diya (5) to Farhan, so Farhan is within two seats of 5: seat 3 or 6. R10 goes from Farhan to Chirag (within two seats). If Farhan = 6, Chirag would have to be at 2 or 3 – neither is within two of 6. So Farhan = 3, Chirag = 2, Eshan = 6.

Seating (going left from Bina): Bina, Aarav, Chirag, Farhan, Gaurav, Diya, Eshan.

Passes: R1 B→A (L1), R2 A→E (R2), R3 E→D (R1), R4 D→?, R5 ?→A, R6 A→F (L2), R7 F→G (L1), R8 G→D (L1), R9 D→F (R2), R10 F→C (R1). For R4–R5 the middle child must be within two seats of both Diya (5) and Aarav (1): Farhan (R2, R2), Eshan (L1, L2) or Bina (L2, L1) – all three possible.

Receivers: R1 Aarav, R2 Eshan, R3 Diya, R4 Farhan/Eshan/Bina, R5 Aarav, R6 Farhan, R7 Gaurav, R8 Diya, R9 Farhan, R10 Chirag. Bina (0 or 1), Eshan (1 or 2) and Farhan (2 or 3) depend on round 4; Gaurav received it exactly once in every case.
